hints: Clear the denominators in the original equation and collect terms to form a three-term quadratic in $u$.
Solve the quadratic and reject any root that cannot equal $e^x$ or makes the original denominator zero.
Take $x=\ln u$ for the admissible root and give exactly 3 decimal places.
walkthrough:
Multiply both sides by the denominator $(\mathrm{e}^x - 3)$, noting $\mathrm{e}^x \neq 3$:
$$\mathrm{e}^x + 2\mathrm{e}^{-x} = 4(\mathrm{e}^x - 3)$$
$$\mathrm{e}^x + 2\mathrm{e}^{-x} = 4\mathrm{e}^x - 12$$

Multiply the entire equation by $\mathrm{e}^x$ to eliminate the negative power $\mathrm{e}^{-x}$:
$$(\mathrm{e}^x)^2 + 2 = 4(\mathrm{e}^x)^2 - 12\mathrm{e}^x$$
$$\mathrm{e}^{2x} + 2 = 4\mathrm{e}^{2x} - 12\mathrm{e}^x$$

Rearrange all terms onto one side to form a three-term quadratic in $\mathrm{e}^x$:
$$4\mathrm{e}^{2x} - \mathrm{e}^{2x} - 12\mathrm{e}^x - 2 = 0$$
$$3\mathrm{e}^{2x} - 12\mathrm{e}^x - 2 = 0$$

Solve the quadratic equation in $\mathrm{e}^x$ using the quadratic formula with $a = 3, b = -12, c = -2$:
$$\mathrm{e}^x = \dfrac{-(-12) \pm \sqrt{(-12)^2 - 4(3)(-2)}}{2(3)}$$
$$\mathrm{e}^x = \dfrac{12 \pm \sqrt{144 + 24}}{6} = \dfrac{12 \pm \sqrt{168}}{6} = \dfrac{12 \pm 2\sqrt{42}}{6} = \dfrac{6 \pm \sqrt{42}}{3}$$

Reject the negative root since $\mathrm{e}^x > 0$ for all real $x$:
$$\mathrm{e}^x = \dfrac{6 + \sqrt{42}}{3}$$

Take the natural logarithm of both sides and round to 3 decimal places:
$$x = \ln\left(\dfrac{6 + \sqrt{42}}{3}\right) = \ln(4.160247) \approx 1.425574$$
$$x = 1.426$$
